headline: Medium risk: shared-document workflows can leak or corrupt content, while prompt-injection risk is low because the prompt-list agent is non-runnable and has no direct ingestion path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable content-writing prompt repository with no I/O surfaces, while agent B is a browser-capable document processor. A direct injection path is not documented, so the only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external reuse of prompt text into B, which is limited and not default.
conditions: IF operator copies prompt text from agent A into agent B as document content, injection becomes possible.
IF agent B is configured to treat pasted text as instructions, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Keep prompt libraries separate from document-processing inputs.
Paste only vetted snippets into agent B.
Add a visible delimiter around imported text.
Review any browser-sourced text before OCR/processing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between prompt sources and document parsers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no network egress, but agent B has allowlisted egress and processes documents/images. If both are pointed at the same workspace or files, B can transmit document contents to its backend or APIs. The shared-workspace pathway is not documented, so uncertainty remains, but the blast radius includes sensitive documents.
conditions: IF agent A and agent B share a filesystem or upload queue, document contents can flow into B.
IF B sends OCR inputs to remote APIs, any sensitive document in that workspace may leave the host.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for A and B.
Do not place sensitive files in B's input directory.
Disable remote API paths in B where possible.
Check which folders B scans before running it.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or network surfaces and agent B only advertises browser/API access, so there is no documented overlapping mutable resource. A conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared writable state not shown in either profile, making the pathway unusual and the blast radius limited to workflow disruption.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflicts become possible.
IF B writes outputs into a location A also edits, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output folders.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Run one agent at a time for the same artifact.
Check for hidden sync folders before processing.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a document-processing system that can consume outputs from agent A, which is a prompt/content-writing source. If B treats A's text as authoritative, errors or fabricated instructions can cascade into OCR/translation outputs or downstream API calls. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text without verification, A's mistakes can propagate.
IF B uses A's output as source material for document transformation, downstream artifacts may inherit errors.
mitigations: Require human review of A's output before B uses it.
Compare B outputs against source documents.
Use checksum or citation checks for imported text.
Separate drafting from transformation steps.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Agent B touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress, while agent A has no egress and no data classes touched. The only compliance concern is a generic one: if regulated documents are processed by B, its remote paths may create policy obligations, but the pairwise mismatch is not proven.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through B's allowlisted egress, policy review is required.
IF the operator expects local-only handling, B's remote paths may violate that expectation.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Keep regulated data out of B.
Review B's retention and logging settings.
Prefer local-only workflows for sensitive files.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees.
